## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Restore the defaults resource before merge because its deletion breaks the existing defaults loader. Other findings concern port validation, hidden configuration failures, and host normalization documentation and coverage.

## Changes
The pull request adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, configuration loading, and host normalization with selected tests. It also deletes the defaults resource and adds reviewer documentation and a fixture.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore the defaults resource — Calling `load_defaults()` after this deletion raises `FileNotFoundError`: `app/startup.py:6` still reads the deleted sibling file. — Callers of the defaults loader can no longer obtain the bundled timeout configuration. — Fix: Restore the resource or update `app/startup.py:6` to supply the defaults without it.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 — For `p=65535`, your validator returns `False` despite documenting the inclusive range 1–65535; the strict upper comparison excludes that valid port. — Callers using this validator reject configurations that select TCP port 65535.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Preserve configuration load failures — For malformed JSON or an unreadable path, your broad handler discards the parsing or filesystem exception and returns `{}`, indistinguishable from a successfully loaded empty configuration. — Users cannot identify or correct a broken configuration because the loader exposes neither the failure nor its cause.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Cover trailing-dot host normalization — For `"Example.COM."`, your new suffix-removal branch has no test coverage; the sole normalization test uses `"Example.COM"` and never enters it. — A regression leaving trailing dots intact would pass the existing host normalization test. — Fix: Extend `test_normalize_host_lowercases` with a trailing-dot input and its expected normalized value.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align the empty-host documentation with the return value — For `h=""`, the docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but your implementation executes `return ""`. — Callers following the documented contract receive an empty string where they expect `None`.
